summary: The selected challenge consists of finding Earth-based analogs for the Moon and Mars. We have created an intuitive website designed for any curious person without programming or science knowledge. Using interactive 3D globes, the user selects an area, adjusts variables explained in simple terms (relief, irradiance, and albedo), and instantly discovers the ten most similar locations on Earth, transforming complex data into visual exploration.
details:
The selected challenge is to find Earth-based analogs for the Moon and Mars. Normally, accessing real surface data from other planets, processing it, and understanding what it means requires highly technical tools, putting this kind of exploration out of reach for most people. Therefore, our main objective has been to democratize this data by developing a visual and intuitive website that brings this information closer to any curious individual, without requiring prior knowledge of programming, data analysis, or planetary science.

Through a clean and interactive interface, users can explore realistic 3D models of the Moon and Mars directly from their browser. With a simple click on any point on their surface—or by entering specific coordinates—they can choose an area of interest and use simple sliders to adjust the weight or importance they wish to give to real physical variables such as relief, solar irradiance, or albedo. Additionally, to encourage learning and comprehension, a brief explanatory summary of each variable's meaning is included right next to it, allowing any user to understand exactly what is being measured without getting lost in technical jargon.

Completely automatically, the system processes these complex parameters behind the scenes and transitions the user to Earth, clearly displaying and ranking the ten terrestrial locations that most closely resemble the selected point. In this way, anyone can visually compare the characteristics of both worlds and move the camera to explore each analogous corner of our planet, transforming hard-to-handle space data into a visual, accessible, and entertaining experience.
The tools we used include Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for programming, with Visual Studio as our development environment. For web Frontend and Backend management, we used Render (for page deployment) alongside Hugging Face Spaces and Datasets (for algorithms and data, respectively). All of this was hosted on GitHub, and we leveraged Antigravity for complex implementations, compare options when selecting our tools.
With this project, Space H has not only handled a key part of the data analysis but has also looked beyond to deliver meaningful value to users. The tool's visual simplicity and ease of use enable a deeper understanding and greater benefit for our target audience, while inspiring the vision and potential to scale it in the future. By making it accessible to users with broader needs, this opens up new horizons for us. This collaboration highlights how transforming complex data into intuitive, user-friendly experiences is more than just a technical achievement—it is a powerful catalyst for long-term scalability and market expansion.
